lines.watchItem: Forward accelerator demand keeps climbing: the four largest US cloud buyers guide to about $725 billion of 2026 capital spending, up 77%, and Google Cloud backlog jumped more than $50 billion in a quarter to $514 billion. Leading-edge wafer-start plans are exposed to how much of that booked backlog converts into real orders.

Advanced packaging is still the gate on realizable GPU revenue, sold out with 52 to 78 week waits and bookings into 2027, though the shortfall has narrowed from roughly 20% to about 10% as capacity runs at 120,000 to 140,000 wafers a month. Watch whether the gap keeps closing or demand re-widens it.

Packaging allocation sits with very few buyers: more than 85% of 2026 and 2027 capacity is pre-booked and one customer holds roughly 60%. That concentration means a single buyer trimming orders leaves capacity that is hard to refill.

Stacked memory, not wafers, now caps how many accelerators ship: suppliers can meet only 60% to 70% of requested volume for the next NVIDIA generation, which has cut its flagship memory from 288GB to 192GB. Wafer and packaging demand can fall short of plan even while end demand stays strong.

The leading-node customer base is tilting toward custom silicon: custom chips are forecast to grow 44.6% against 16.1% for merchant GPUs in 2026, hyperscaler in-house parts pass $25 billion, and MediaTek has raised its accelerator share target to 15-20%. The mix of who books leading-node capacity is shifting even as total volume grows.

A second merchant source is real but late: AMD data-center revenue doubled to $6.7 billion and its rack reached production with third-quarter shipments, yet one supply-chain account puts first production output at the second quarter of 2027. The timing of that ramp shapes how much second-source volume lands in 2026 versus 2027.

Sellers still set prices across the chain, with TSMC gross margin at 67.7% and NVIDIA holding 75%, but memory suppliers are taking a growing share as server memory contract prices rise more than 25% in a quarter and rack component costs climb 2% to 3% a week. Watch whether rising input costs start eating into what buyers will pay for finished systems.

Packaging work is starting to travel: Google has ordered more than 3 million units of Intel bridge packaging for its next custom chip, Intel claims yields above 90% at about half the cost, and rival routes quote 26 to 39 week waits against 52 to 78. The competing route has its own limits, being better suited to custom chips than to high-bandwidth accelerators.
